content.title: What is a Monotonic Stack?
content.description: A Monotonic Stack is a stack that maintains its elements in either increasing or decreasing order while processing data.

content.content: The Monotonic Stack Pattern is one of the most important optimization techniques in Data Structures and Algorithms. It helps solve problems involving nearest greater, nearest smaller, previous greater, previous smaller, and range-based queries efficiently.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: Many medium and hard interview questions that appear to require O(n²) solutions can be optimized to O(n) using a Monotonic Stack.
Why Do We Need Monotonic Stacks?
Suppose for every element you want to find the next greater element on the right. A brute-force solution checks all future elements, resulting in O(n²) complexity.

content.title: Key Observation
content.content: Every element enters and leaves the stack at most once, leading to linear complexity.
Types of Monotonic Stacks
How Monotonic Stack Works
When processing a new element, we remove stack elements that violate the monotonic property. This guarantees the stack always remains ordered.
Application 1: Next Greater Element
The Next Greater Element (NGE) problem asks for the first larger element to the right of every element.

content.title: Solution Strategy
content.description: Use a decreasing stack and process elements from right to left.

content.content: Application 2: Next Smaller Element
This problem finds the first smaller element appearing after the current element.

content.title: Solution Strategy
content.description: Use an increasing stack and remove larger elements.

content.content: Application 3: Previous Greater Element
Previous Greater Element finds the nearest larger value on the left side of every element.
Application 4: Stock Span Problem
The Stock Span problem calculates how many consecutive days before today had prices less than or equal to today's price.

content.title: Interview Favorite
content.content: Stock Span is one of the most frequently asked Monotonic Stack interview problems.
Application 5: Daily Temperatures
For every day, determine how many days must pass until a warmer temperature occurs.
Application 6: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
This advanced problem finds the largest rectangular area that can be formed within a histogram.

content.title: Advanced Application
content.content: Histogram Area is considered one of the most important Monotonic Stack problems for interviews.

items.question: Why is my answer wrong?
items.answer: You may be using the wrong stack direction.

items.question: Why is complexity high?
items.answer: Avoid nested loops and trust stack popping.

items.question: Should I store values or indices?

content.title: Important Interview Tip
content.content: For most Monotonic Stack problems, storing indices is often more useful than storing values because indices help compute distances and ranges.

content.title: Interview Insight
content.description: Whenever a problem asks for nearest greater/smaller elements, previous/next relationships, spans, or range boundaries, think Monotonic Stack immediately.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Increasing stacks help solve smaller-element problems.
Decreasing stacks help solve greater-element problems.
Every element is pushed and popped at most once.
Most solutions run in O(n) time.
Stock Span uses a decreasing stack.
Daily Temperatures uses a monotonic stack.
Histogram Area uses previous and next smaller elements.
Monotonic Stack is a top interview pattern.
